key_insight: Reformulates statistical watermarking using e-values to produce the first anytime-valid detection procedure, and introduces a principled way to choose sampling distributions to improve detection power while allowing valid early stopping.
problem_solved: Overcomes two limitations of prior watermarking: (1) ad-hoc sampling distributions that reduce power, and (2) fixed-horizon tests that break validity under optional stopping, preventing reliable early detection.
method: Builds an e-value based test statistic for watermark detection so hypothesis tests remain valid under optional stopping (anytime-valid inference).
Develops principled criteria for selecting sampling distributions that optimize detection power under the watermarking scheme.
Provides algorithms with theoretical guarantees and empirical evaluations on LLM-generated text to demonstrate improved power and valid early stopping.
impact: Enables practitioners to detect machine-generated text more reliably and efficiently—using fewer tokens and allowing safe early stopping—while retaining provable statistical guarantees, improving practicality for real-world deployment and monitoring.
